label: Efficient and total cause of a thing's being r: a CAUSE_2 cause whose causing needs no co-cause
definition: `TotalCauseIn F Total c x r` holds exactly when F.CausesIn c x r (c is a cause of x's being r, CAUSE_2 of the grades frame) and Total c x r: c's causing of x's being r is total, it needs no co-cause alongside c. The contrast is a partial cause (concausa), one that produces the effect only together with others. Total is a primitive binder; TotalCauseIn conjoins it with the frame's cause relation, so that every total cause is a cause by definition and nothing else about Total is assumed.
note: Analyst stipulation, attribution deferred (navigation: Descartes, Meditation III, 'the efficient and total cause'; the Second Replies axiom speaks of the 'first and adequate' cause, which is not formalized here). Example: a fire that alone heats water is a total cause of its heat; a spark that ignites a fuel whose stored energy produces the explosion is a partial cause of the explosion's energy. Exclusions: total is not sole (two total causes of one effect are not excluded), not first (a total cause may itself be caused) and not modal sufficiency. Open obligation: no law relates Total to CausesIn, InAct or MoreIn beyond the conjunction; the frame lacks a co-cause relation from which Total could be defined.
